message:
## Vulnerability Digest

Four relevant vulnerability clusters were newly published in the last 24 hours: one critical Docker Sandboxes issue, Mozilla's high-impact Firefox release advisories, and two consolidated groups of Ubuntu security notices. Immediate review is recommended for Docker Sandboxes on macOS and Firefox deployments.

**Scope**

- Sources: `Products.txt` and `List_of_SIA_Completed.txt` only; obvious aliases were normalized and duplicate entries were merged.
- `DLL_software_component.txt` was not read or combined with this scan.
- Window: 2026-09-15 05:10 IST through 2026-09-16 05:10 IST (2026-09-14 23:40 UTC through 2026-09-15 23:40 UTC).
- Date-only items published on September 14 were excluded when their exact time could not be verified inside the rolling window.

**Finding 1 - Docker Desktop / Docker Sandboxes on macOS**

- **Issue:** CVE-2026-77179
- **Severity:** Critical, CVSS 4.0 score 9.4
- **Description:** Docker's virtio-fs host server can follow a replaced parent directory symlink when reopening an unlinked file. A malicious sandbox guest can escape the shared workspace and read or modify files available to the VMM user, potentially leading to host code execution.
- **Why relevant:** The monitored inventory explicitly includes Docker Desktop. The issue affects Docker Sandboxes on macOS and was assigned by Docker.
- **Sources:** [CVE record](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-77179); [Docker Sandboxes v0.42.0 release](https://github.com/docker/sbx-releases/releases/tag/v0.42.0)

**Finding 2 - Mozilla Firefox and Firefox ESR multiple vulnerabilities**

- **Issue:** Mozilla Foundation Security Advisories MFSA 2026-90 through MFSA 2026-93; the advisories enumerate CVE-2026-92005 through CVE-2026-92079 with edition-specific subsets.
- **Severity:** High overall; individual issues range from high to low.
- **Description:** Mozilla fixed numerous use-after-free, privilege-escalation, sandbox-escape, boundary-check, information-disclosure, spoofing, mitigation-bypass, and denial-of-service flaws in Firefox 156 and Firefox ESR 115.41, 140.16, and 153.3.
- **Why relevant:** Mozilla Firefox is explicitly monitored. The four advisories were announced on September 15, 2026, and overlapping CVEs across Firefox editions are consolidated here.
- **Sources:** [Firefox 156 advisory](https://www.mozilla.org/en-US/security/advisories/mfsa2026-90/); [Firefox ESR 115.41](https://www.mozilla.org/en-US/security/advisories/mfsa2026-91/); [Firefox ESR 140.16](https://www.mozilla.org/en-US/security/advisories/mfsa2026-92/); [Firefox ESR 153.3](https://www.mozilla.org/en-US/security/advisories/mfsa2026-93/)

**Finding 3 - Ubuntu user-space security notices**

- **Issue:** USN-8770-1, USN-8769-1, USN-8768-1, USN-8767-1, USN-8766-1, USN-8765-1, USN-8762-1, USN-8764-1, and USN-8763-1
- **Severity:** No single overall severity is stated by Canonical.
- **Description:** Canonical published fixes for SimpleSAMLphp, phpseclib, Shibboleth, Snapcast, Suricata-Update, python-sql, polkit, SRT, and kitty. Reported impacts include sensitive-information exposure, SQL injection, arbitrary file writes, denial of service, content injection, and possible code execution or administrator-level execution.
- **Why relevant:** Ubuntu is explicitly monitored. Each notice names supported Ubuntu releases and was published on September 15, 2026.
- **Source:** [Canonical Ubuntu Security Notices](https://ubuntu.com/security/notices?offset=0&order=newest)

**Finding 4 - Ubuntu Azure and NVIDIA kernel vulnerabilities**

- **Issue:** USN-8761-1, USN-8730-2, and USN-8760-1
- **Severity:** No single overall severity is stated by Canonical.
- **Description:** Canonical released Ubuntu 24.04 and 22.04 kernel updates for Azure and NVIDIA variants, covering a large set of security defects across networking, filesystems, drivers, memory management, and other kernel subsystems. USN-8730-2 specifically addresses CVE-2026-53131; the two larger notices enumerate their complete CVE sets on the vendor pages.
- **Why relevant:** Ubuntu is explicitly monitored. The three notices were published on September 15, 2026; overlapping kernel CVEs are consolidated rather than repeated.
- **Sources:** [USN-8761-1](https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8761-1); [USN-8730-2](https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8730-2); [USN-8760-1](https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8760-1)

**MongoDB ecosystem sweep**

A dedicated sweep covered MongoDB Server Community and Enterprise, mongod, mongos, Atlas and Atlas services, Ops Manager, Cloud Manager, Compass, mongosh, Database Tools, Kubernetes Operator, official drivers and connectors, BI Connector, Charts, Realm/App Services, official integrations, and major maintained libraries and services. MongoDB's newest first-party alert was dated September 11, 2026; no credible MongoDB ecosystem finding was newly published or updated within this run's 24-hour window.

**Review priority**

Prioritize Docker Sandboxes on macOS and Firefox/Firefox ESR because the vendor-reported severity reaches critical and high. Review the applicable Ubuntu notices against deployed releases and kernel variants; Canonical does not assign one aggregate severity to those notice groups.
